topic.title: Proposing Attribute Values from an External Database

body.p: In some cases, an attribute value references an external database (for example, a citation or product number). You can configure to propose only values that are valid in that database (for example, valid product numbers or article references).

You can set the attribute value in the Attributes side-view or with an inline form control, such as a combo box. By default, a combo box provides the same options as the Attributes side-view: the valid attribute values defined in the schema associated with the XML document.

There are several ways to implement this:
Use a cc_config.xml configuration file for your custom framework to configure the values that are proposed for an attribute in the Attributes side-view.
Use the JavaScript sync.actions.AttributeEditingActionsProvider API to implement a widget that will be presented in the Attributes side-view to allow the user to choose a value for an attribute.
Customize to propose custom values for an attribute by using the SchemaManagerFilter Java API. This server-side implementation can cache values across multiple documents.
For DITA documents, if a Subject Scheme map is referenced in the root DITA map, it will be used when proposing values for an attribute. If having a static map with possible attribute values is not flexible enough, you can use the ro.sync.exml.workspace.api.editor.page.ditamap.keys.KeyDefinitionManager API class. It has a getEnumerationDefinitions method that can be used to return possible values for an attribute.
Implement a custom form control that connects to the external database to propose choices to the user. In this form control, you can fetch the options on-demand, which may be useful for large databases. An example of a custom form control is available on GitHub.Your external database needs to have an HTTP API with CORS enabled to be able to query it from .
